correctness.rationale: Every product in the claimed domain has commutator equal to the classical Witt bracket. Therefore every algebra isomorphism is a Witt Lie automorphism. Bavula's complete automorphism theorem reduces it to the maps \(W_n\mapsto\varepsilon a^nW_{\varepsilon n}\). Exact comparison of the constant, m, and n coefficients then forces \(q=q'\) and \(\mu=\varepsilon\lambda\), with explicit converse maps. The automorphism group follows by setting \(\mu=\lambda\). The proof covers all integers m,n and all complex parameters in the stated domain; finite verification is only supplementary.

value.rationale: The recent classification introduces q as a deformation parameter and organizes the Witt products fiberwise. Whether q survives after forgetting the q-pre-Lie label is the natural global moduli question. Proving that distinct q-fibers never merge turns q from a presentation parameter into an intrinsic invariant of the underlying multiplication; the automorphism jump at lambda=0 also identifies the unique enhanced-symmetry stratum. This is structural information about the full new family rather than a routine numerical specialization.
